techniques.mechanism: Blackwell 5th-gen tensor cores: one thread issues a whole-tile MMA, accumulating in Tensor Memory instead of registers, at several times the mma.sync / wgmma throughput
risks: descriptor / swizzle-mode mistakes give silent wrong results
TMEM alloc/dealloc must be balanced per CTA
needs TMA or cp.async.bulk for feeding

realizations.how: tcgen05.mma.cta_group::1 with A/B from shared-memory descriptors (swizzled 128B layout), accumulator in TMEM allocated with tcgen05.alloc, completion via tcgen05.commit -> mbarrier; epilogue reads TMEM with tcgen05.ld into registers. Needs -arch=sm_100a (already the build flag). Keep the mma.sync kernel as the fallback for shapes that miss alignment.

techniques.mechanism: two CTAs of a cluster issue one MMA over a doubled tile (e.g. 256xN), halving B-operand traffic per FLOP

realizations.how: cluster of 2 CTAs, tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2, leader CTA issues, each CTA loads its half of A and shares B via multicast TMA.

techniques.mechanism: TMA-multicast one tile to several CTAs of a cluster so L2 is read once

realizations.how: launch with a cluster dim (cudaLaunchKernelEx + cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension), cp.async.bulk.tensor ... .multicast::cluster with a CTA mask; mbarrier expect_tx covers all receivers.

techniques.mechanism: one CTA per SM loops over output tiles so the epilogue of one tile overlaps the loads of the next and tail waves vanish

realizations.how: grid = #SMs; each CTA walks tile ids tile += gridDim.x (or a stream-K / grouped order); double-buffer the accumulator (two TMEM or register sets) so the epilogue overlaps the next mainloop.

techniques.mechanism: XOR-swizzle the shared-memory tile address instead of padding so ldmatrix / cp.async / TMA accesses are bank-conflict free and tiles stay 16B-aligned
risks: write and read swizzles must match

realizations.how: address = row*BK + ((chunk ^ (row & mask)) << 3) for 16-byte chunks, applied identically on the cp.async write and the ldmatrix read; on sm_90+ use the TMA 32/64/128B swizzle modes.

techniques.mechanism: retune the CTA tile (BMxBNxBK) and warp tile to the SM's shared-memory / register budget: larger tiles raise arithmetic intensity until occupancy or spills bite

realizations.how: try 128x256x32 (warp 64x64), 256x128x32, BK=64, 4-5 stages; check registers (<=255), shared memory (<= the per-SM budget in the hardware block) and that M/N divisibility still holds (keep a fallback).

techniques.mechanism: remap CTA ids (grouped / swizzled rasterization) so CTAs running at the same time share A and B tiles in L2

realizations.how: pid -> (group of GROUP_M=8 row-tiles, column-major inside the group) as in grouped GEMM; costs a few integer ops per CTA.

techniques.mechanism: write the accumulator tile to shared memory and store 16-byte rows (coalesced), fusing bias / activation there

realizations.how: after the mainloop reuse the pipeline smem as a padded C tile, __syncthreads, then each thread copies uint4 rows to global; on sm_90+ use a TMA store.

techniques.mechanism: load the next k-slice's operand fragments (ldmatrix) while the current slice's MMAs issue, hiding shared-memory latency

realizations.how: keep two register fragment sets; at slice kk issue ldmatrix for kk+1 (and the next tile's kk=0 after the stage wait) before the mma loop for kk.

techniques.mechanism: when output tiles do not fill all SMs, split K across CTAs (split-K / stream-K) and reduce the partials

realizations.how: assign each CTA a K-range of a tile, accumulate in fp32 workspace (or atomics / a second kernel) and convert to fp16 once; stream-K balances the tail.
